items.title: Houthi missile attack damages Aramco administration building in Riyadh
items.summary: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted ballistic and cruise missiles early Sunday, but falling debris damaged an Aramco office building in Riyadh; the Houthis claimed the attack. Saudi officials reported no casualties, and no refinery, pipeline or crude-production outage has been established. This widens regional infrastructure risk alongside Hormuz shipping attacks, but does not yet demonstrate an additional physical oil-supply loss.

observations.value: 2 ballistic missiles and 2 cruise missiles targeting Riyadh and other regions; attribution to Houthis

observations.label: Confirmed damage
observations.value: Aramco administrative building in Riyadh financial district; Saudi Energy Ministry described falling debris damage; no reported casualties

observations.label: Production/refining/pipeline throughput impact
observations.value: No disruption verified; administrative facility, not confirmed production installation

observations.label: Market move at observation time
observations.value: No corroborated post-incident oil or equity-price response established; US regular-session markets closed Sunday

items.key_finding: Direct damage to an Aramco office highlights Houthi escalation risk, but there is no evidence yet of additional oil-production disruption.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly secures $3.4 billion of gas-fired generation commitments for AI data centers
items.summary: The Financial Times reports Anthropic took over commitments for 1.7 GW of Caterpillar gas-fired generators originally ordered by OnePWR, in a deal agreed in late September and disclosed November 8. Reuters independently reported the FT account but said it could not verify it. This is a significant power-supply bottleneck signal, not evidence of a new Caterpillar equipment order.

observations.value: Sunday, November 8, 2026; transaction reportedly agreed in late September

observations.label: Reported deal size
observations.value: Approximately $3.4 billion

observations.label: Reported generator capacity
observations.value: 1.7 GW of gas-fired generation commitments

observations.label: Equipment manufacturer and order provenance
observations.value: Existing Caterpillar generator orders placed by OnePWR around 2024; not demonstrated to be incremental CAT orders

observations.label: Independent transaction confirmation
observations.value: Not established; Reuters explicitly could not immediately verify the FT report

observations.label: Public equity price response
observations.value: No new US regular-session trading on Sunday

items.key_finding: AI developers may be assuming direct power-equipment procurement to bypass multi-year grid and generator lead times; reported deal remains single-source.

items.title: Separate outbound tanker reportedly struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: UKMTO Warning 200-26, reported November 8, describes a tanker struck by an unknown projectile while sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz on November 7. The company security officer reported that the crew were safe and no environmental impact was known. This is distinct from the Khasab tanker fire and Gulf of Oman bulker strike already in the feed; the attacker and incremental oil-flow impact remain unverified.

items.title: US military disables commercial bulk carrier attempting to cross Iran blockade
items.summary: US Central Command says it disabled the St Kitts and Nevis-flagged bulk carrier Huda in the Gulf of Oman on November 7 after repeated warnings during an attempted departure following a visit to an Iranian port. This is a material escalation in direct enforcement of the US maritime blockade. The event does not establish an additional oil-supply outage; monitor retaliatory action, ship routing and insurance costs.

items.title: Tanker fire near Khasab prompts crew evacuation amid persistent Hormuz shipping risk
items.summary: UKMTO Warning 199-26 reports a tanker on fire approximately eight nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman, on November 7; military authorities reported that the crew evacuated. The warning was issued on November 8 as a delayed report. The cause, vessel identity, casualties, pollution and any additional oil-throughput loss are not confirmed; avoid attributing the fire to a particular belligerent without evidence.

observations.label: Location
observations.value: Approximately 8 nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman

observations.value: Tanker on fire; crew evacuated

observations.label: Cause and physical petroleum-flow impact
observations.value: Unconfirmed; no independently established incremental throughput loss

items.key_finding: A new tanker evacuation demonstrates ongoing acute vessel risk near Hormuz, but does not establish a new oil-volume shock.
